newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 15.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 15.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
LONDON - The government plans to publish a draft bill soon for an effective ban on tobacco advertising as part of a drive to reduce smoking in Britain.
TOKYO - Sony Corp says it will boost its stake in Tokyu Agency International Co, a medium-sized advertising agency, to 94 percent from the current 12.5 percent.

LONDON - British advertisers have used toilet walls, eggs and even airline sick bags to promote their products, but now comes perhaps the most unusual ad space so far -- sportsmen's noses. Soft drink company Britvic will advertise its Red Card brand on nasal strips worn by Chelmsford City Football Club.
PARIS - French cosmetics giant L'Oreal has signed up supermodel Claudia Schiffer to add a touch of glamour to its mass market hair care line Elseve.

LONDON - Kellogg Europe consolidates its media buying into a newly formed company that is part of J. Walter Thompson. Kellogg Europe, part of U.S.-based Kellogg Co, the world's largest cereal maker, previously bought its advertising space through six different companies but will now use just one company called Kellogg Europe Media.
MUNICH - International news and information organisation Reuters Holdings Plc and French media company Havas launch a data service for the advertising and media industry called Adways Data.
BONN - German Justice Minister Edzard Schmidt-Jortzig calls for a unified code of advertising regulations in Europe, saying the current system fails to provide sufficient direction for the industry.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

TOKYO - Media tycoon Rupert Murdoch expresses a strong interest in developing the digital broadcasting business in China, which he says is leap-frogging the analogue era and going directly to digital technology.

NEW YORK - Walt Disney Co's ABC News division says it will unveil its foray into the Internet news arena with ABC.news.com, a 24-hour online news service squarely aimed at competing with MSNBC, the joint venture between NBC and Microsoft Corp.

NEW YORK - Greenhouse Networks, the original content developer of America Online Inc, says its Santa home page will make the leap to national television this winter, the first time an original online brand will become a television feature.
SEOUL - South Korea's Doosan Dong-A Co says it has signed a contract with Conde Nast International of the United States to launch the Korean edition of the women's magazine Glamour.

LONDON - The management of leading British pop group Oasis is threatening legal action for breach of copyright against hundreds of unofficial Internet sites dedicated to the band, the Financial Times reports.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Food group Groupe Danone aims to double sales outside France to 30 billion francs ($5.3 billion) by 2000. Its priority zones are Latin America, Asia and central Europe. It aims to double "Danone" brand sales in the next five years from the current 23 billion francs through internal growth and acquisitions.

PAWTUCKET, Rhode Island - Hasbro Inc says that privately held Lucasfilm Ltd has extended its licensing agreements with the company to make Star Wars toys, games, puzzles and related products through 1998.
MOSCOW - General Motors takes its second leap into Russian car production with plans to build a new car in the country by the end of 1998 together with Finnish and Russian partners.
LONDON - British household products group Reckitt & Colman says it is confident that the underlying momentum of 1996 will continue.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - British consumers are flocking to eat at themed restaurants, where the food often plays second fiddle to the atmosphere and T-shirt sales contribute as much to profits as the menu, market research company Mintel says.

NEW DELHI - Indian wallets are getting heavier these days, and it's not just due to cash. Plastic money has firmed its grip as the traditionally credit-averse Indian consumer has taken quickly to the buy-now-pay-later idea, industry experts say.

LONDON - Asia's 20-something generation is following a distinctive path, blending traditional Asian values with aspects of Western lifestyles, a report from ad agency Ogilvy & Mather says. Asian values -- such as hard work, humility, thrift and respect for the family -- endure and there is little sense of crass materialism and moral decline it says.

RABAT - Morocco plans to recycle old vehicles in a new polyester body for use in the country's remote rural areas, the official MAP news agency says. "The car is the result of recycling old vehicles, which makes it cost less than other vehicles," MAP says.
